profile_text.body:
Thinking Machines Lab is an artificial intelligence research and product company, described on its site as a for-profit startup founded in 2025 and headquartered in San Francisco, California. The company says it is building toward a future where everyone has access to the knowledge and tools to make AI work for their own needs and goals. It identifies three gaps it intends to address: scientific understanding of frontier AI systems lagging behind their capabilities, knowledge about how such systems are trained being concentrated within top research labs, and the difficulty people face in customizing these systems to their own needs and values.

The company describes its staff as scientists, engineers, and builders who have worked on AI products including ChatGPT and Character.ai, open-weights models such as Mistral, and open source projects including PyTorch, OpenAI Gym, Fairseq, and Segment Anything. It states that it plans to publish technical blog posts, papers, and code, and that it favors multimodal systems built for human-AI collaboration over fully autonomous systems, AI that adapts across fields of expertise rather than only programming and mathematics, frontier model intelligence in domains such as science and programming, and an empirical approach to safety that combines proactive research with real-world testing, red-teaming, and post-deployment monitoring.

The company's recorded profile lists no products and no MCP servers. No lawsuits are listed against it. Its legal exposure is recorded in California, with a count of 270.
